title: RWB-S9-E6032-APP: no source publishes an override operation, an override element or a reason property, no rule row or decision code names the placement override, the instruction status list has no published transition table, the two screens give the override no state and name no action, the legacy permission table gives right U while the operation declares C and its 21 and 5 further holders are not enumerated, and no requirement row traces to FEAT-PRM-04
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R5.7, R7.2, R7.3 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S9-E6032-APP; context pack S9 rwb-partner (service row, ownership rows: tables partner, partner_instruction and partner_user, 6 REST operations, EV-20 and EV-21, workflow InstructionWorkflow, no job; Architecture v5 slides 2, 4, 5, 8 and 12); legacy RWB-E6-032; FSD S9 Partner management v3 A1.2, A1.3, A1.4, A2.4, A2.4.2, A2.4.3.1 to A2.4.3.3 and A2.4.4; TSD S9 Partner management v2 T1, T2, T3.0 to T3.3, T5.2, T5.3, T6.1, T6.2, T8, T-A.1 and T-A.2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 Rules, Route sets and States sheets; Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-20 and EV-21; API Specification v4 components InstructionRequest, PartnerInstruction, Partner and DecisionLogEntry; Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row FEAT-PRM-04
description: (1) The legacy story lets the partner manager place work differently and no source publishes an operation for it: TSD S9 T-A.1 and the context pack give six operations, of which API-S9-002 POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions with right C is the only one that places work, and the two endpoints the legacy story lists (a read of the caller's instructions and a result post) place none; the override is therefore read as a branch of API-S9-002 (ASM-B2-S9-005-2). (2) The reason the legacy criterion asks for has no published field of its own: FSD S9 A2.4.3.2 gives the partner fields and the two instruction keys only, TSD S9 T3.1 gives partner_instruction nine columns with no reason, and InstructionRequest carries instructionType, partnerId and dueOn only, while DecisionLogEntry.overrideReason is the published home of a reason taken against a recommendation (ASM-B2-S9-005-2, ASM-B2-S9-005-3). (3) No rule row of the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 names the override: the rows that re-place work are R-LIT-29, R-DIS-31, R-WO-35 and R-UNI-45, each firing on a partner step of its own route set, and the decision code vocabulary of DecisionLogEntry is D5.1 to D9.3, X1 to X7 or an access event, so the rule ID, the rule set and the decision code of this step carry the placeholder (ASM-B2-S9-005-4). (4) TSD S9 T3.2 publishes LOV-INSTR-STATUS SENT, ACCEPTED, DECLINED, IN_PROGRESS, DONE and RECALLED and no source publishes the transition table of that list, so only the two moves of this step are stated (ASM-B2-S9-005-1). (5) The legacy screen table gives SCR-35 Placement and allocation and SCR-34 Partner list the state Loading; list, and neither source says where the override action sits or what fields the dialog carries (ASM-B2-S9-005-7). (6) The legacy permission table gives Partner portal right U to eight roles and 5 more, and 21 more roles hold R, while TSD S9 T-A.1 declares right C on API-S9-002 and T6.1 gives C to seven identities; the difference is recorded and the matrix is not widened (ASM-B2-S9-005-6). (7) TSD S9 T8 maps REQ-S9-001 to REQ-S9-004 and REQ-S9-008 to FEAT-PRM-01 and REQ-S9-005 to REQ-S9-007 and REQ-S9-009 to FEAT-PRM-08, and the legacy story carries no REQ id, so the story cites no requirement (ASM-B2-S9-005-9).
evidence: TSD S9 T-A.1 (6 operations, API-S9-002 Partner portal C, first in E4) and T-A.2 (InstructionRequest, PartnerInstruction, Idempotency-Key, errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503); TSD S9 T3.1 (DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016, no reason column) and T3.2 (four lists); API Specification v4 InstructionRequest (instructionType, partnerId, dueOn), PartnerInstruction (9 properties, 6 required) and DecisionLogEntry.overrideReason (maxLength 1000); FSD S9 A2.4.3.2 and A2.4.3.3; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-LIT-29, R-DIS-31, R-WO-35 and R-UNI-45; legacy RWB-E6-032 Data, Endpoints, Screen and states and Permission checks; TSD S9 T8
owner_role: Business lead; solution architect; rwb-decision rule owner; rwb-access owner
proposed: Serve the override as the branch of the published API-S9-002 with one additive optional overrideReason property, record the reason and the rule version in the local decision record before the change, end the replaced partner_instruction at RECALLED and create the replacement at SENT, take right C over the operation matrix and record the wider legacy U as a difference, place the action on SCR-35 in its list state behind the composite route, keep the case, the clock and the officer assignment with rwb-case, and hold the rule ID, the decision code, the transition table and the requirement row as open items.

title: RWB-S9-E6032-CON: InstructionRequest publishes no override property and no source gives the override an element, the required flags of the request are not published, no rule row or decision code names the placement, TSD S9 T5.3 and the Event and Messaging Design disagree on the direction of EV-21 while the pattern set carries no DP-09, the legacy permission table gives U while the operation declares C, and no requirement row traces to FEAT-PRM-04
source: Template and Rules v1 R4, R5.4, R5.5, R7.2 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S9-E6032-CON; context pack S9 rwb-partner (service row, naming rules, ownership rows, Architecture v5 slides 5, 8 and 12); legacy RWB-E6-032; FSD S9 Partner management v3 A2.4.2, A2.4.3.1 to A2.4.3.3 and A2.4.4.4; TSD S9 Partner management v2 T0, T1, T2, T3.0 to T3.3, T5.2, T5.3, T6.1, T6.2, T8, T-A.1 and T-A.2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-LIT-29, R-DIS-31, R-WO-35 and R-UNI-45; Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-20 and EV-21; API Specification v4 components InstructionRequest, PartnerInstruction and DecisionLogEntry; Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row FEAT-PRM-04
description: (1) The API Specification v4 publishes InstructionRequest with instructionType, partnerId and dueOn and no reason property, and no source publishes an override element, an override flag or an override path, so the baseline adds one optional overrideReason with the name and the 1000-character length of the published DecisionLogEntry.overrideReason and declares no second reason property and no override entity (ASM-B2-S9-005-2, ASM-B2-S9-005-3). (2) The published InstructionRequest carries no required list while PartnerInstruction requires six of its nine properties, so the request's own required flags carry the placeholder and the override branch declares the three fields it needs (ASM-B2-S9-005-2). (3) No rule row or decision code of the Routing Logic set names the placement override and the DecisionLogEntry decision code vocabulary does not hold a placement code, so the consumed row's operation name, the rule ID and the decision code carry the placeholder (ASM-B2-S9-005-4). (4) TSD S9 T5.3 lists InstructionIssued and PartnerResultSubmitted as Published while the Event and Messaging Design v4 gives EV-20 the direction Published and EV-21 the direction Consumed; the conflict is recorded, no direction is declared here, and the pattern set carries no DP-09 although the service owns a topic (ASM-B2-S9-005-5). (5) TSD S9 T-A.1 declares right C on API-S9-002 and T6.1 gives C to seven identities, while the legacy permission table gives right U to eight roles and 5 more and records 21 more holders of R without naming them (ASM-B2-S9-005-6). (6) TSD S9 T8 maps no requirement to FEAT-PRM-04 and the legacy story names none, so the baseline carries no requirement (ASM-B2-S9-005-9).
evidence: API Specification v4 InstructionRequest (3 properties, no required list), PartnerInstruction (9 properties, required id, caseId, partnerId, instructionType, instructedAt, status) and DecisionLogEntry.overrideReason (maxLength 1000); TSD S9 T-A.1 and T-A.2; TSD S9 T3.0 to T3.2 and T5.3; Event and Messaging Design v4 rows EV-20 and EV-21; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-LIT-29, R-DIS-31, R-WO-35 and R-UNI-45; legacy RWB-E6-032 Permission checks; TSD S9 T6.1 and T8; split plan slice RWB-S9-E6032-CON (C empty, patterns DP03, DP13, DP19)
owner_role: Solution architect; rwb-partner tech lead; business lead; rwb-decision rule owner; rwb-access owner
proposed: Publish the override branch inside API-S9-002 with the published InstructionRequest plus one additive optional overrideReason, the PartnerInstruction answer with its nine properties, six required flags and four lists, the rule row as a class C consumed row with a fake and no rule row, no override element, no event, no second topic and no Schedule, the partner-portal right C with the seven holders of T6.1 and the legacy U recorded as a difference, and hold the request's required flags, the rule ID, the decision code, the transition table and the requirement row as open items.
